title: Building an inference stack that improves itself
gist: Not an inference provider but a customer-service AI company tuning its own endpoints. An orchestrator replays redacted production traffic, profiles, and spawns sub-agents that must each return an explanation, an intervention, a prediction and a test that could falsify it. Confirmed gains become the new baseline.
changes: The first case here of the loop being run by the workload's owner on its own traffic, not by a provider. It is the closest thing to a user-workload-aware stack, and it lives on rented cloud GPUs.
caveats: Unverifiable. Each row uses a different baseline, so the gains do not add. The largest come from known levers (quantisation, n-gram speculation), not new engine work. People start the loop and approve deployment.

numbers.metric: Requests/s per GPU within the latency SLA, 8-bit weights plus n-gram speculation
Draft model adapted to own traffic

bears_on.note: One company, its own traffic, its own loop. The like-for-like part (the adapted drafter) is 1.34x.
Sub-agents must state a falsifiable prediction before a change is accepted.
The user owns the workload and the loop, but not the hardware.
Replayed production traffic is the evaluation rig.
